humanAcceptance.evidence: Dave approved through the current authorized owner Telegram channel after immutable artifact 9023055533 became available. His selected response was: 'Approve this exact preview and publish Pass 69.1'. This binds publication authorization to preview pr-preview-53-139a753dd11658a3855832d73b1222308f1b0e24 at source SHA 139a753dd11658a3855832d73b1222308f1b0e24. Dave had stated that he would test the mobile feel more properly later, so this records exact publication approval and does not claim hands-on preview inspection.

requirements.summary: Mobile thumbsticks acquire through their complete visible discs and emulate normalized gamepad axes
requirements.expected: Move and aim engage from the centre knob, inner disc, edge and diagonals; the visible fixed-origin disc maps to circular -1..1 axes and uses the same applyRadialDeadzone curve as physical gamepad sticks.
requirements.falsifier: A centre-knob press is ignored, an inner press only works near the edge, diagonal magnitude exceeds one, or touch and physical-gamepad radial shaping diverge.

evidence.note: Pure centre, inner, edge and diagonal projections use the physical-gamepad radial deadzone helper and remain circularly bounded.
A real captured pointer acquires through each centre knob, then drives live player movement and camera yaw before clean release.
The approved immutable preview contains the fixed visible stick discs exercised at 320x667, 390x844 and 844x390.

requirements.summary: FIRE is beside the right aim stick without overlapping other mobile controls
requirements.expected: FIRE is the final visual and focus-order control and remains within one practical thumb gap of the right aim stick in narrow portrait, portrait and landscape while every hit region remains distinct.
requirements.falsifier: FIRE is farther than the bounded thumb gap, overlaps the aim stick or another button, steals another pointer, leaves the viewport, or has focus order inconsistent with its visual order.

evidence.note: The retained three-viewport collision matrix reports zero intersections and a FIRE-to-aim edge gap no greater than 24 CSS pixels.
Immutable-preview screenshots show FIRE immediately above the portrait aim stick and immediately left of it in landscape.

requirements.summary: Bidirectional mid-match rotation recovers without crash and releases held touch ownership
requirements.expected: Portrait-to-landscape and landscape-to-portrait changes keep the current match active, coalesce renderer/camera sizing, clear held FIRE and stick state, preserve advancing frames and leave controls usable; ordinary internal renderer resizing does not clear touch input.
requirements.falsifier: Rotation emits a page error, strands or duplicates the match, leaves held input latched, loses controls, stops frame advancement, or adaptive pixel-ratio/support-camera resizing incorrectly releases touch input.

evidence.note: One active match rotates in both directions while movement, aim and FIRE pointers are held in turn; each orientation recovers active phase, centres held sticks, clears triggerHeld, advances frames, retains controls and emits zero page errors.
Viewport events call recoverViewport while established internal resize callers retain the geometry-only coalesced resize path.

requirements.summary: Gun Field Kit restores canonical DPS without duplicating stale balance UI
requirements.expected: The selected-primary inspector contains one DPS row calculated as base damage times pellets times RPM divided by 60, followed by Damage, Fire Rate, Range and Control; AK-47 displays 350.
requirements.falsifier: DPS is absent, duplicated, hard-coded independently of the weapon registry, uses a non-canonical formula, clips, or AK-47 projects a value other than 350.

evidence.note: The shell retains one five-stat inspector including DPS while the weapon-card cyclic-DPS catalog projection remains canonical.
The served custom AK-47 inspector displays one visible DPS row with value 350 and remains bounded across retained desktop widths.
The immutable preview screenshot visibly shows DPS 350 in the selected AK-47 panel.

requirements.summary: The player-facing static or asset-backed image note is removed
requirements.expected: Weapon previews remain accessible and weapon-specific without rendering the ASSET-BACKED STILL badge or equivalent implementation-note copy.
requirements.falsifier: ASSET-BACKED STILL, STATIC-BACKED IMAGE or equivalent player-facing copy remains in source, built bytes or the Field Kit DOM, or preview alt text becomes inaccessible.

evidence.note: The served Field Kit rejects the retired badge text while every weapon-specific preview image loads.
Visual inspection of the immutable preview shows no asset/static-backed badge.

requirements.summary: The corrected live route is player-facing version 69.1
requirements.expected: The live chooser, runtime identity and changelog show The Big One v69.1 while the protected internal acceptance lane remains PASS 69 and Stable Pass 67.1 plus Rollback Pass 63 retain their pinned source topology.
requirements.falsifier: The live card/runtime still presents v69, channel labels disagree, Stable or Rollback provenance changes, or the release infrastructure is weakened merely to admit a decimal internal pass number.

evidence.note: The staged production chooser presents PASS 69.1 / THE BIG ONE v69.1 and retains byte-pinned Stable and Rollback routes.

requirements.summary: Ctrl+Shift+R recovery guidance is visible before selecting a game version
requirements.expected: Candidate and staged production version choosers visibly tell the player to press Ctrl+Shift+R when the selected version did not update, at desktop and narrow widths.
requirements.falsifier: The guidance exists only inside Options, loads after channel selection, clips at a retained width, or is absent from staged production-shell bytes.

evidence.note: The front chooser requires visible Ctrl+Shift+R guidance before navigating to a channel.
The immutable preview screenshot shows the guidance directly below the version cards.

requirements.summary: The Options hard game refresh is available on the front version chooser
requirements.expected: HARD RESET / REFRESH clears every CacheStorage entry and reloads the current chooser with a fresh cachebust parameter before a version is selected.
requirements.falsifier: The button is decorative, performs an ordinary reload, leaves seeded cache entries, navigates to a channel, loses the chooser, or is absent from the staged production shell.

evidence.note: The test seeds a cache, activates the front button, observes a changed cachebust URL, proves the cache was deleted and confirms the chooser remains visible.
The immutable preview visibly exposes HARD RESET / REFRESH beside the Ctrl+Shift+R note.

requirements.summary: Retained Pass 69 gameplay and protected release topology do not regress
requirements.expected: Existing FIRE, held automatic FIRE, USE, PAUSE, pointer cancellation, portrait/landscape layout, gameplay properties, build/provenance contracts and pinned Stable/Rollback channels remain intact outside the explicit correction surfaces.
requirements.falsifier: A retained Pass 69 unit/property/browser contract fails, an unrelated release channel changes source, touch FIRE regains pointer-lock coupling, USE or PAUSE breaks, or exact-head build/provenance validation fails.
